intro: Septic and sewer workers run heavy equipment and monitor systems in tough conditions. The closest of the 25 careers below is construction equipment operation, with an 89% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $59,850, which is 20% more than the $49,880 septic and sewer workers earn.
why_it_works: The job means operating vacuum trucks and jetters, finding blockages and keeping systems working safely. O*NET rates operation and control at 3.88 out of 5 for this job and operations monitoring at 3.62. Equipment operation, earth drilling, oil field work and pipelaying use the same skills. Almost every match needs no extra schooling. The gaps are operations analysis and equipment maintenance.
tips: Earth drillers earn $60,190, which is 21% more, and are an 85% match.
Locomotive Engineers earn $81,410, or 63% more, and railroads train new hires.
Oil and gas rotary drill operators earn $67,890, which is 36% more, often with travel.

faq.q: What jobs can former septic and sewer workers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are construction equipment operators (89%), surface mining excavating operators (87%) and Pipelayers (86%), based on O*NET 31.0. Earth drillers are 85% matched and earn $60,190, which is 21% more than the $49,880 septic and sewer median.

faq.q: Which careers for septic and sewer workers pay more?
faq.a: 16 of the 25 matches pay more. Locomotive Engineers earn $81,410 (63% more), Pile Driver Operators $73,300 (47% more) and oil and gas rotary drill operators $67,890 (36% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Oil field jobs often involve travel and long shifts.

faq.q: Do septic and sewer workers need more education to switch?
faq.a: Rarely. 23 of the 25 matches need no more education than septic tank servicers and sewer pipe cleaners already have, including all of the top 10. In the closest match, 82% of workers have a high school diploma or the equivalent.

faq.q: What skills should septic and sewer workers learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are operations analysis, equipment maintenance, equipment selection and programming. Repairing already rates 3 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so maintaining machines is the main step toward better-paid equipment and drilling jobs.
